To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) bone is a target organ of diabetes, 2) the effects of diabetes and glucose-lowering drugs on bone are mediated by glucose metabolism and glucose oxidative derivatives, and 3) diabetes affects bone by impairing bone remodelling, bone material quality, bone microvascular function, bone stem cell niches and fracture healing.

diabetes is associated with a number of bone disorders and that the effects of diabetes and its treatment on bone are mediated through multiple mechanisms, including impaired bone remodelling, defective bone material properties and impaired bone microvascular function.

diabetes causes bone fragility and that bone is affected by diabetes via impairments of bone microvascular function, muscle endocrine function, glucose metabolism, and toxic effects of glucose oxidation products.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cellular and molecular basis of diabetes bone syndrome, and the potential of diabetes bone syndrome as a target for the development of new glucose-lowering therapies.
the cellular and molecular mechanisms that link diabetes to skeletal fragility.
understanding the cellular and molecular mechanisms that contribute to bone fragility in diabetes and how this might be targeted therapeutically.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
diabetes has a detrimental effect on bone, but the precise mechanism remains to be elucidated.
bone is affected by diabetes, and this may be mediated by a number of mechanisms.
diabetes is associated with bone fragility, and that the bone fragility of diabetes is a consequence of the disease itself, and not a consequence of the treatment of diabetes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
diabetes and bone are intimately linked and that bone fragility in diabetes is a multifactorial process.
diabetes has a detrimental effect on bone health and bone quality, but that the effects of glucose-lowering therapies on bone are complex, and may vary depending on the underlying disease mechanism.
bone is affected in both types 1 and 2 diabetes and that the bone effects are mediated by glucose metabolism, AGEs, and by impairments in bone vascular and muscle endocrine functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

bone health in diabetes can be improved by targeting the cellular and molecular pathways that underlie bone fragility, and that the same pathways can be targeted to improve bone and muscle health, and to improve glucose homeostasis.
diabetes has profound effects on the skeleton and bone cells, and that these effects are not limited to the osteoblast lineage.
diabetes is a disease of bone and that bone fragility is a consequence of the disease.
